- When sentiment is negative and price is trending upward, model tends to overestimate — reduce forecast slightly.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility — dampen forecast slope.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in downward trends — if price drops sharply, forecast should not fall below 10–15% below recent low.
- In high-sentiment volatility periods, model overfits recent noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days unless sentiment strongly confirms trend.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment > 0.10.
- Forecast should not diverge more than 3% from 14-day moving average unless sentiment strongly supports outlier direction.
